name: Process Definition Service
purpose: Define processes that are managed by the platform, Versioned Process Catalog, Stores schemas and rules for process(es). Provides versioned validation configuration, versioned UI bundle, and versioned label configuration for process definitions.

internal_components.name: Process Definition API
internal_components.responsibility: Exposes endpoints to create, update, publish, retrieve, and list versioned process definitions, including schemas, rules, validation configuration, UI bundles, and label configuration.

internal_components.name: Process Definition Application Service
internal_components.responsibility: Coordinates process definition lifecycle use cases, including draft management, version creation, publication, retrieval, and validation of commands against domain rules.

internal_components.name: Process Definition Domain
internal_components.responsibility: Encapsulates business rules for process definition versioning, publication state transitions, schema consistency, and integrity of validation, UI bundle, and label configuration artifacts.

internal_components.name: Process Definition Repository
internal_components.responsibility: Persists and retrieves versioned process definitions, metadata, publication status, and associated configuration artifacts.

internal_components.name: Process Definition Event Publisher
internal_components.responsibility: Publishes process definition lifecycle events when a process schema version is published or updated.

security_controls: Role-based access control for creating, updating, publishing, and reading process definitions
Authentication and authorization enforced on all service endpoints
Audit logging for process definition creation, modification, publication, and access to versioned artifacts
Input validation and schema validation for all submitted definition payloads
observability: Structured application logs for API requests, lifecycle actions, validation failures, and event publication
Metrics for request rates, error rates, publish operations, update operations, and persistence latency
Distributed tracing across API, application, persistence, and messaging components
